stages.name: Outside the war
stages.desc: Alpine peoples beyond the reach of both Rome and Carthage

stages.name: Roman-held
stages.desc: Rome, its colonies and its Italian allies

stages.name: Carthaginian-held
stages.desc: Hannibal's last strongholds in the south

stages.name: Gauls & Ligurians
stages.desc: Independent tribes, hostile to Rome and courted by Carthage

stages.name: Hasdrubal's march
stages.desc: Lands crossed by Hasdrubal Barca's army, 207 BC

stages.name: Mago's campaign
stages.desc: Lands held or raided by Mago Barca's army, 205–203 BC

states.name: Valle d'Aosta
timeline: The Salassi, Alpine Celts who guard the passes, owe nothing to Rome

states.name: Piemonte
timeline: Taurini and other Ligurian and Gallic tribes of the upper Po, beyond Roman control
Hasdrubal comes down from the Alps with his Gallic recruits, unopposed
Hasdrubal's army is gone; the tribes of the upper Po are left to themselves

states.name: Lombardia
timeline: The Insubres, the greatest Gallic people of the Po valley, enemies of Rome since 218; Rome holds the colony of Cremona
Insubrian warriors join Hasdrubal's march down the Po
After the Metaurus the Insubres wait, still hostile to Rome
Mago fights two Roman armies in the land of the Insubres and is badly wounded

states.name: Trentino-Alto Adige
timeline: Raetian peoples of the Alpine valleys, outside the war

states.name: Liguria
timeline: Ligurian hill tribes; the port of Genua is friendly to Rome
Mago lands from the Balearics, takes Genua and allies with the Ingauni
Mago recruits Ligurians and Gauls with Carthaginian silver
Wounded, Mago falls back to the Ligurian coast, where Carthage's envoys recall him

states.name: Emilia-Romagna
timeline: Country of the Boii, hostile to Rome; Rome holds the colonies of Placentia and Ariminum
Hasdrubal besieges Placentia in vain, then marches down the Aemilian plain past Ariminum
The Boii remain hostile; Rome's colonies hold on

states.name: Marche
timeline: The Ager Gallicus, Roman since 283, with the colony of Sena Gallica
Hasdrubal's army is caught and destroyed on the Metaurus river
Roman again: the danger in the north is over

states.name: Veneto
timeline: The Veneti and the Cenomani, Rome's loyal allies north of the Po

states.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
timeline: Carni and other Alpine peoples at the head of the Adriatic, outside the war

states.name: Abruzzo
timeline: Marsi, Paeligni and Marrucini, Rome's Italian allies
Nero's column hurries north along the Adriatic coast

states.name: Molise
timeline: Samnite country, back in Rome's alliance
Nero's men pass Larinum on their forced march north

states.name: Apulia
timeline: Rome holds Apulia and has retaken Tarentum; Hannibal still raids it
Nero's camp near Canusium faces Hannibal; Hasdrubal's head is thrown before his outposts

states.name: Basilicata
timeline: Lucania and Metapontum: Hannibal's lands; Marcellus is killed in an ambush on its edge
After the Metaurus, Hannibal evacuates Metapontum and his Lucanian allies

states.name: Calabria
timeline: Bruttium: Hannibal's base, with Locri and Croton
Hannibal pulls back into Bruttium, his last corner of Italy
Scipio retakes Locri; Hannibal records his deeds at the temple of Hera Lacinia
Recalled by Carthage, Hannibal sails from Croton for Africa

states.name: Campania
timeline: Capua, Hannibal's great ally, retaken and punished by Rome in 211

states.name: Lazio
timeline: Rome, at war with Carthage for a decade
Rome celebrates its first triumph of the war for the Metaurus

states.name: Toscana
timeline: Etruria, Rome's wealthy but restless ally, watched by a Roman army
Rome tries Etruscan nobles accused of plotting with Mago

states.name: Sicily
timeline: A Roman province, the granary of Rome's armies
Scipio trains the army that will invade Africa
Scipio sails from Lilybaeum for Africa

states.name: Sardegna
timeline: A Roman province since 238
Mago dies of his wound at sea off Sardinia

states.name: Umbria
timeline: Umbrian towns allied to Rome, and the colony of Narnia on the road to Rome
Hasdrubal's captured letter names Umbria as the place to meet Hannibal

events.title: Battle of Baecula
events.text: Scipio attacks Hasdrubal Barca's hill camp; Hasdrubal saves his treasury, his elephants and most of his army.

events.title: Scipio at New Carthage
events.text: Scipio's base since he stormed the city in 209; he does not pursue Hasdrubal north.

events.title: Over the Pyrenees
events.text: Hasdrubal leads his army into Gaul, probably by a western pass, and winters there.

events.title: Massalia warns Rome
events.text: Rome's Greek ally reports that Hasdrubal is in Gaul and recruiting.

events.title: Marcellus killed
events.text: Both consuls ride into an ambush near Venusia; Marcellus is killed, Crispinus mortally wounded.

events.title: Locri relieved
events.text: Hannibal drives off a Roman siege of Locri, a key port of Bruttium.

events.title: Hannibal in Bruttium
events.text: After ten years in Italy, Hannibal holds only the far south.

events.title: The Arverni join
events.text: Gallic peoples, the Arverni among them, swell Hasdrubal's army.

events.title: Over the Alps
events.text: Hasdrubal crosses the Alps in spring, far faster than his brother did in 218.

events.title: Siege of Placentia
events.text: Hasdrubal loses precious weeks besieging the Roman colony, then gives up.

events.title: Battle of Grumentum
events.text: The consul Gaius Claudius Nero checks Hannibal in Lucania.

events.title: The letter intercepted
events.text: Four Gallic and two Numidian riders carrying Hasdrubal's letter are caught by Roman foragers near Tarentum.

events.title: Nero's secret march
events.text: Nero slips out of his camp near Canusium with 6,000 picked infantry and 1,000 cavalry.

events.title: Fed along the road
events.text: Towns on the route bring food, horses and volunteers to Nero's column.

events.title: Porcius falls back
events.text: The praetor Porcius Licinius shadows Hasdrubal from Ariminum toward Sena.

events.title: Two consuls at Sena
events.text: Nero joins his colleague Livius Salinator by night, sharing the same camp to hide his arrival.

events.title: Battle of the Metaurus
events.text: Lost by the river, Hasdrubal is brought to battle; his army is destroyed and he dies charging the Romans.

events.title: Hasdrubal's head
events.text: Back at Canusium, Nero has Hasdrubal's head thrown before Hannibal's outposts.

events.title: Retreat to Bruttium
events.text: Hannibal gathers his allies from Metapontum and Lucania and withdraws to Bruttium.

events.title: Triumph in Rome
events.text: Livius rides in triumph; Nero, whose march won the battle, rides beside him on horseback.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio defeats Hasdrubal son of Gisco and Mago; Carthaginian Spain collapses.

events.title: Repulsed at New Carthage
events.text: Mago tries to surprise New Carthage from the sea and is driven off.

events.title: Gades shuts its gates
events.text: Shut out of Gades, Mago has its magistrates flogged and crucified.

events.title: Scipio visits Syphax
events.text: Scipio sails to the Numidian king Syphax at Siga to win him for Rome.

events.title: Winter in Minorca
events.text: Repelled from Majorca by its slingers, Mago winters on Minorca and recruits two thousand islanders.

events.title: Genua taken
events.text: Mago lands with about 12,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry and takes Genua by surprise.

events.title: Alliance with the Ingauni
events.text: Mago joins the Ingauni Ligurians in their war on a mountain tribe.

events.title: Reinforcements from Carthage
events.text: Carthage sends Mago 6,000 infantry, 800 cavalry, seven elephants and money to hire Gauls.

events.title: Locri retaken
events.text: Scipio seizes Locri from Hannibal's garrison.

events.title: Hannibal's inscription
events.text: At the temple of Hera Lacinia, Hannibal sets up a bronze tablet recording his campaigns.

events.title: Scipio in Sicily
events.text: As consul, Scipio trains an army of volunteers and exiles for Africa.

events.title: Etruria under suspicion
events.text: Rome investigates Etruscan nobles accused of conspiring with Mago.

events.title: Scipio lands in Africa
events.text: Scipio crosses from Lilybaeum and lands near Utica.

events.title: Fighting near Croton
events.text: The consul Sempronius fights Hannibal in Bruttium without decision.

events.title: Battle of the Great Plains
events.text: Scipio and Masinissa defeat Hasdrubal son of Gisco and Syphax.

events.title: Syphax captured
events.text: Masinissa takes Syphax prisoner and occupies Cirta.

events.title: Battle in Insubria
events.text: Two Roman armies defeat Mago in the land of the Insubres; he is wounded in the thigh.

events.title: Mago recalled
events.text: On the Ligurian coast, envoys from Carthage order Mago home.

events.title: Death at sea
events.text: Mago dies of his wound off Sardinia; many of his ships are taken by the Romans.

events.title: Hannibal leaves Italy
events.text: After fifteen years in Italy, Hannibal sails from Croton for Africa.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Italy, by who held each of today's regions. A simplification: regions are today's boundaries, control was often patchy, and the passage of an army through a region marks it for that year only. Dates follow Livy and Polybius.
